gloss: to chase, to pursue, to run after

definitions.explanation: To follow someone or something quickly in order to catch them.
To seek or strive for something such as a goal, dream, or career.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}が{猫|ねこ}を{追|お}い{掛|か}けた。
{子|こ}どもたちが{友|とも}だちを{追|お}い{掛|か}けている。
examples.english: The children are chasing their friend.

examples.japanese: {泥棒|どろぼう}を{追|お}い{掛|か}けて{捕|つか}まえた。
examples.english: I chased the thief and caught him.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}が{逃|に}げた{犯人|はんにん}を{車|くるま}で{追|お}い{掛|か}けた。
examples.english: The police chased the escaped criminal by car.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}り{遅|おく}れそうになって、ホームを{走|はし}って{追|お}い{掛|か}けた。
examples.english: He was about to miss the train, so he ran along the platform chasing after it.

examples.japanese: {夢|ゆめ}を{追|お}い{掛|か}けている。
{目標|もくひょう}を{追|お}い{掛|か}けて{毎日|まいにち}{頑張|がんば}っている。
examples.english: I am working hard every day pursuing my goal.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}は{音楽|おんがく}の{道|みち}を{追|お}い{掛|か}けていた。
examples.english: When I was young, I was pursuing a career in music.

examples.japanese: {理想|りそう}ばかり{追|お}い{掛|か}けていても、{何|なに}も{始|はじ}まらない。
examples.english: Nothing will happen if you just keep chasing ideals.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{家族|かぞく}の{反対|はんたい}を{押|お}し{切|き}って、{自分|じぶん}の{夢|ゆめ}を{追|お}い{掛|か}け{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: She kept pursuing her dream despite her family's opposition.

notes:
{追|お}い{掛|か}ける is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) meaning to chase or pursue.

COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
- {追|お}う (to chase) + {掛|か}ける (to hang on, to start) → to keep chasing

ASPECT (ている):
{追|お}い{掛|か}けている indicates an ongoing chase or pursuit.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {犯人|はんにん}を{追|お}い{掛|か}ける (chase a criminal)
- {夢|ゆめ}を{追|お}い{掛|か}ける (pursue a dream)
- {目標|もくひょう}を{追|お}い{掛|か}ける (pursue a goal)
- {追|お}い{掛|か}けっこ (a game of chase/tag)

VARIANT:
- {追|お}いかける: same verb, sometimes written without {掛}

RELATED WORDS:
- {追|お}い{越|こ}す: to overtake (catch up and pass)
- {追|お}い{掛|か}ける focuses on the act of chasing, not necessarily catching

[Register: Neutral]
